title: Canary: the Gate G2 loss curve still reproduces at HEAD
hypothesis: Re-running the Gate G2 loss-curve experiment at HEAD regenerates the committed loss-curve.summary.csv to within float round-off. If it does not, a code change altered a seeded stream or the training numerics, and every number produced after that change is on a different stream from every number before it.

config.freeze: none: both world models train on every step

toleranceBasis.why: The reference was produced in the loop's sandbox; CI runs on a different CPU. tfjs-node's oneDNN kernels order float operations differently per CPU, so the two are not bit-identical even with identical code and seeds.
toleranceBasis.observedIn: CI run 42657621834 (GitHub ubuntu-latest), 2026-11-09, with src/ identical to the reference run's commit: 476 of 600 loss cells differed, none by more than this.
toleranceBasis.crossSeedBasis: Between the reference's own seeds (1001, 1002, 1003), compared cell by cell over the four non-constant loss columns: no cell of 160 per pair is within 1e-6. The median above is the lowest of the three pairwise medians. A different seeded stream therefore fails this card on every cell, not marginally.
toleranceBasis.chosen: 1e-6: about 20 times the observed machine round-off and about 45 times below the smallest difference between two streams.

decisionRule.text: Pass if the regenerated loss-curve.summary.csv has the same rows and columns as the committed reference and every numeric cell is within maxDifference of it, where the difference between a and b is |a - b| / max(1, |a|, |b|). A NaN halt is a fail. The tolerance and the measurements it rests on are in config.toleranceBasis.

onFail: Find the commit that changed the stream: git bisect with `npm run exp -- 0000 --scratch --require-pass`. If the change was intended, say so in the PR that makes it and add a new canary card with a new reference. Do not edit this card or its reference.
